newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Premier's popularity at new low - poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Premier's popularity at new low - poll.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson has scored the lowest popularity rating ever given to a premier by pollster IMU/Testologen, in a survey marking his first 12 months in office.
Persson, who heads the minority Social Democratic government, got 2.4 points out of a possible five in a poll of 1,008 Swedish adults published on Tuesday in the daily Aftonbladet.

"It is the worst rating a prime minister has received so far in IMU/Testologen's polls," the paper said. "It is particularly sad for Goran Persson that the rating has fallen continously since he became prime minister," it added.
In a survey by the pollster in June last year, Persson's approval rating was 2.7, just before Christmas it was 2.6 and in March it was 2.4.

The decline in his personal standing measured by IMU/Testologen was in line with other polls showing dwindling support for the Social Democratic party as a whole since it took power in the autumn of 1994.
Last week, a poll by Temo showed backing for the Social Democrats, who will fight to retain office in September 1998 general elections, at its lowest since April 1991.
It showed support from 26.5 percent of voters, down from 45 percent in the 1994 general election.

Traditional party supporters are alarmed at former finance minister Persson's economic austerity programme which has cut welfare and social spending across the board in an effort to balance the national budget.
